_contract: Amendment 1 to the INTERPRETATION of the CUDA stage-F engineering validation. It corrects two explanatory claims and nothing else. It does not alter any observed device field, any subrun cost, any provider identity, any PASS/FAIL outcome, or any scientific interpretation, and it rewrites no raw subrun report, no campaign record, no provider evidence and no historical execution record. It is APPEND-ONLY: the artifacts it corrects are bound below by content hash and left exactly as written. AUTHORIZES NOTHING.
written_by: post-CUDA evidence and reproducibility closure, on reporting commit 573d6cfc92497c176afe4645335df1a2534f93df
binding_rule: sha256 over the exact bytes of each corrected artifact at the time this amendment was written. A later edit to any of them breaks the binding, which is the point: an interpretation amendment must not silently attach itself to different evidence.

corrections.subject: cuda_stage_f_20260910_s2
corrections.why: The suffix computations COMPLETED. Every one of the eight matrix cases reported applied=true and raised no error. What failed was the acceptance criterion the harness applied to them: it required the operator's CHILD to be on the requested compute device. `initialization/device.py` documents the opposite as the builder's contract -- ChildBuilder does not place the model, so a parent on CUDA routinely coexists with a freshly built child on the host. On CPU the criterion was vacuously true, because device=cpu satisfied it by construction; the first real GPU is where a wrong question first got a wrong answer. This was a defect in the measuring instrument, not in the operator under test.

corrections.subject: cuda_stage_f_20260910_s3
corrections.was: wording that reads as though every operator left its child on the requested CUDA device
corrections.why: That is the contract the run actually observed and the one the corrected criterion checks: the operator COMPUTES on the requested device, and the child it returns is host-resident because the builder does not place it. Saying the children were left on CUDA would describe a different system and would make the corrected criterion look wrong.
